reason: This passage (Joshua 2) describes Joshua sending two spies to scout Canaan and their encounter with Rahab in Jericho. There is no depiction of the Hebrew people suffering greatly, nor do any leaders address the people assigning blame for suffering. The passage focuses on military reconnaissance and covenant-making. Rahab mentions YHWH's positive acts on behalf of Israel (the crossing of the Red Sea and victories over Amorite kings), not situations of suffering. The only distress mentioned is the fear of the Canaanites regarding the approaching Israelites.
